column1: ETHICS BANK · Moral courage and presence of mind under duress
column2:
Capt. Smit Machchhar, flydubai FZ1073 (Dubai–Tel Aviv), Sept 2026. Stabbed by his co-pilot, who allegedly tried to crash the plane, he still released the cockpit door so passengers could overpower the attacker. All 174 people on board landed safely at Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. President Murmu cited his 'presence of mind'.
Use: duty above self-preservation; courage as acting despite fear; values tested in crisis, not in comfort.
Pair with: Neerja Bhanot (Pan Am 73, 1986; Ashoka Chakra).
Src: TH 2 Oct 2026, p1, p14

column1: ETHICS BANK · Institutional accountability vs individual blame
column2:
Indore (Bhagirathpura) water contamination, Dec 2025–Feb 2026: 30+ deaths (22 officially linked). The judicial commission (Justice S.K. Gupta) called it preventable, a 'cumulative consequence of failures… over several decades'. It found tender delays of 859+ days, sewer lines laid above water pipes, and records 'missing' with no destruction register.
Use: diffusion of responsibility ('many hands'); record-keeping as an accountability tool; the gap between rankings ('cleanest city' 8 years running) and basic service delivery.
Src: TH 2 Oct 2026, p5

column1: ETHICS BANK · Conflict of interest and the duty to disclose
column2:
CEC Appointment Act case (SC, Sept 2026): an application says Justice S.C. Sharma did not disclose that his son was the EC's standing counsel. The applicant expressly alleges no actual bias, only that non-disclosure took away the chance to seek recusal. (Pending; cite as a question raised, not a finding.)
Use: justice must be seen to be done; disclosure is owed even where there is no actual bias.
Pair with: nemo judex in causa sua; Bangalore Principles of Judicial Conduct (2002), impartiality.
Src: TH 2 Oct 2026, p15

column1: ETHICS BANK · Conscientious objection and constitutional morality
column2:
Vande Mataram made penal (2026): hearing T.M. Krishna's challenge, Justice Bagchi observed that a person who stands respectfully but does not sing should face no criminal consequence. That is the Bijoe Emmanuel (1986) principle.
Use: respect cannot be compelled ('a prayer compelled is no prayer'); constitutional morality protects dissent; patriotism as conduct, not posture.
Src: TH 2 Oct 2026, p11 (Sanjay Hegde op-ed)

column1: ETHICS BANK · Empathy, compassion and the dignity of the weakest
column2:
Thinker line: Narsinh Mehta's 'Vaishnava jana to tene kahiye, je peed parai jaane re': the truly good person is one who feels another's pain as their own. It was Gandhi's daily prayer.
Counter-example: Bhadohi (UP), Sept 2026. A Musahar woman (Musahars are an SC community) was denied admission and gave birth by the roadside. An official inquiry found four doctors and a nurse guilty of 'serious negligence'; the family alleges caste prejudice.
Use: empathy as a public-service value; Gandhi's talisman.
Src: TH 2 Oct 2026, p11, p16

column1: ETHICS BANK · Procurement ethics: lowest price vs value and safety
column2:
Counterfeit-drug rackets, Delhi 2026: doctors and patient advocates blame the rule that public hospitals buy from the lowest bidder (L1), which lets cheap and spurious medicines in. One doctor: 'a 50% discount should raise suspicion'. A thalassemia patient took ineffective fake iron chelators for a year.
Use: economy vs effectiveness; the duty of care in procurement; Quality-and-Cost-Based Selection over pure L1; the harm is to people who cannot verify what they receive.
Src: TH 2 Oct 2026, p8

column1: ETHICS BANK · Ethics of science and research
column2:
Xenocortication (Stanford, Nature, Sept 2026): human brain organoids grew to fill about 92% of the cortex in mice. The team consulted bioethicists before starting and argued that grafts into embryos or non-human primates need greater scrutiny first. There is no evidence of a human-like mind, but bigger grafts raise questions about animal cognition and moral status.
Use: the precautionary principle; ethics review placed before the experiment; 'can' vs 'should'.
Pair with: the 3Rs of animal research (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement).
Src: TH 2 Oct 2026, p22

column1: ETHICS BANK · VIP culture vs citizen-first public service
column2:
Assam, Oct 2026: an ambulance carrying a critically ill patient was stopped to let the CM's convoy pass, and the patient died the next day. The CM disputed any link to the halt but stated the norm himself: 'no inconvenience should be caused to people due to his or any Minister's movement'.
Use: power as trust; access to services before status; norms must change practice, not just speeches.
Pair with: the 2017 red-beacon ('lal batti') ban.
Src: TH 2 Oct 2026, p4
